tekst: De drukregelaar verlaagt de waterdruk tot een stabiele druk die onafhankelijk is van de inlaatdruk van de watertoevoer. De vereiste inlaatdruk van de watertoevoer ligt tussen 1,0 en 6 bar. De drukregelaar wordt tijdens een espressocyclus ingesteld op een uitlaatdruk van ca. 0,8 - 0,9 bar. De invoer- en uitvoerleiding van de regelaar moeten in de juiste richting zijn aangesloten. In tegenovergestelde richting werkt de regelaar niet goed. Aan de kant van de regelaar zit een pijl die de juiste waterstroomrichting aangeeft. De regelaar heeft een terugstroombeveiliging. Deze terugstroombeveiliging voorkomt de mogelijkheid dat water vanuit de machine terug in de watertoevoer stroomt. Procedure voor het aanpassen van de Voer de volgende stappen uit: druk 1. Verwijder de onderste plaat van de achterkant van de machine. 2. Verwijder plug P1 (zie inzet). ▪ Zie het binnenaanzicht van het Heetwatersysteem (op pagina 28) voor meer informatie. 3. Sluit de manometer aan op de slang. 4. Trek de knop uit om de regelaar te ontgrendelen. 5. Selecteer een (dubbele) espresso. 6. Pas de regelaar aan door de knop tijden de pompcyclus van de espressoselectie te draaien. ▪ De manometer moet tijdens een espressocyclus tussen de 0,8 - 0,9 baraangeven. ▪ Met de klok mee draaien => verhogen van uitvoerdruk (vanaf boven gezien) ▪ Tegen de klok in draaien => verlagen van uitvoerdruk 7. Vergrendel de regelaar door de knop naar beneden te drukken. 8. Ontkoppel de manometer en doe de plug in de slang. 9. Plaats de achterplaat op de machine. 10. Klaar.
bron: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

tekst: De waterstroommeter (waterteller) meet de hoeveelheid water die door het heetwatersysteem stroomt. Drie functies zijn gebaseerd op de waterstroommeter: 1. De waterdosering voor consumpties is gebaseerd op de hoeveelheid pulsen die de waterstroommeter genereert. 2. Tijdens de opstartprocedure wordt gedetecteerd of er water in het systeem stroomt. Is dat niet het geval dan stopt de machine en worden de foutmeldingen “opstartprobleem” en “geen water aangesloten” weergegeven. 3. Hoeveel de boiler verwarmt is, naast het meten met de temperatuursonde, ook gebaseerd op de hoeveelheid inkomend water. De waterstroommeter zit tussen de drukregelaar en de pompen ingebouwd. Het is een kleine turbine die elektrische pulsen afgeeft. Elke rotatie van 360º produceert 2 pulsen in de sensor (Hall- element). De pulsen worden door het regelsysteem gedetecteerd. De leiding naar de waterstroommeter moet in de juiste positie worden aangesloten; de waterstroommeter kan geen water detecteren in tegenovergestelde richting. Er staat een kleine pijl op de waterstroommeter die de juiste richting aangeeft. De waterstroommeter is een 1,8 mm-type. Elke puls is ongeveer 0,8 ml water. tekst: De pompen genereren de druk en stroming van het water. De pompen verhogen de druk naar de vereiste brewingdruk (tussen 1,5 en 10 bar). De pomp is een vibratiepomp. De zuiger vibreert op en neer om druk op te bouwen. De pomp is een 24VAC-pomp. Het elektrische signaal naar de pomp is een 24V-blokgolf. De druk kan door het elektrische signaal (pulsbreedte) naar de pomp worden aangepast. Een langere puls zorgt voor een hogere druk omdat de zuiger verder omhoog gaat. De maximale pulsbreedte is 20. Dit getal kan voor elke consumptie apart in het onderhoudsprogramma worden ingesteld. Vanwege de hoge frequentie van de pulsen kan dit elektronische signaal niet met een gewone spanningsmeter worden gemeten. De pulsen voor de twee pompen bewegen uit fase, waardoor een stabiele hoge druk ontstaat voor het zetten van een espresso. tekst: Temperatuurbeveiliging / clixon De temperatuurbeveiliging (of clixon) beschermt de verwarming tegen oververhitting als het regelsysteem de verwarming niet uitschakelt. De beveiliging onderbreekt de stroomtoevoer naar de verwarming onmiddellijk als de boiler te heet wordt. De beveiliging is een behuizing met een bimetalen schijf. Als het apparaat te heet wordt, opent de bimetalen schijf een (in rusttoestand gesloten) schakelaar. Interne delen van de temperatuurbeveiliging 1. Schakelarm 2. Transferpin 3. Basis 4. Schijfbevestiging 5. Kap 6. Bimetalen schijf Na het afkoelen kan de veiligheidsschakelaar worden gereset door handmatig op de pin (1) te drukken. Waardes temperatuurbeveiliging Deze koffiemachine heeft één open boiler en één drukboiler. De open boiler heeft twee verschillende clixons. • Een droogkookbeveiliging op het bovendeksel van de open boiler. Deze clixon schakelt uit wanneer de temperatuur boven de 110 °C ± 5 °C uitkomt. • Een temperatuurbeveiliging op de overloopleiding van de open boiler. Deze clixon schakelt uit wanneer de temperatuur van het overtollige water boven de 90 °C ± 5 °C uitkomt. De drukboiler heeft twee identieke clixons. • Deze zitten beide aan de zijkant van de drukboiler. Ze schakelen uit wanneer de temperatuur boven de 110 °C ± 5 °C uitkomt.

tekst: Het 2 bar-drukventiel is een mechanisch drukventiel. Dit ventiel opent als een druk van 2 bar is bereikt. Als het systeem in stand-by staat, wordt het overstortventiel geactiveerd (geopend) als de verwarmingselementen worden ingeschakeld. De maximale druk in het systeem is tijdens stand-by dan ook 2 bar.

tekst: Algemeen De D-molen heeft high-performance maalschijven die consistent malen en die voor het malen van bonen voor koffie en espresso twee keer sneller werken dan de Schaerer-molen. Dit betekent dat in de helft van de tijd dezelfde hoeveelheid koffie kan worden gemalen. Zie de specificaties aan het einde van dit hoofdstuk voor meer informatie. De D-molen is eenvoudig schoon te maken en de instellingen (zoals de maalgrofheid) blijft behouden als de molen voor reiniging wordt geopend. De maalgrofheid van de D- molen wordt niet door pinnen of tanden gemeten, maar wordt op een indicatiescherm op de molen weergegeven. Op het indicatiescherm is een schaal van 0 tot 12 te zien (werkelijke grofheid gedeeld door 10). De D-molen staat af fabriek standaard op een maalgrofheid van 6. Let op: door het soort gebruikte bonen en de (lokale) smaakvoorkeuren kan het zijn dat de instellingen van de molen in de koffiemachine moeten worden aangepast. OPMERKING Bestaande recepten/configuraties met koffie moeten worden gewijzigd als de D-molen wordt gebruikt terwijl ze voor de Schaerer-molen gemaakt zijn (vanwege meer uitgifte van gemalen koffie). 1. Schroef 10. Motoraandrijving molen 2. Bovenstel molenhuis 11. Instelschroef maalgrofheid 3. Bovenste maalschijf (stilstaand) 12. Schaalvenster maalgrofheid 4. Schroef bovenste maalschijf 13. Afstelkap molen 5. Schroeven onderste maalschijf 14. Schroeven wormwiel 6. Onderste maalschijf (roterend) 15. Afstelwiel 7. Molenbasis / Motorafdekking 16. Molenuitlaat 8. Molenhouder 17. Aandrijfas 9. Molenhuis 18. Onderstel maalschijf De molen bestaat uit een bovenstel (2) met daarin de stilstaande (niet-bewegende) bovenste maalschijf (3). Het bovenstel is op het molenhuis vastgezet met een bayonetsluiting voor gemakkelijke toegang. In het molenhuis (9) zit het onderstel met de roterende onderste maalschijf (6). Door de onderste maalschijf naar onder en boven te verstellen, kunt u de luchtopening tussen de twee maalschijven zeer nauwkeurig instellen. De opening tussen de twee maalschijven bepaalt de grofheid van de gemalen koffie, ook wel de maalgrofheid genoemd. De maalgrofheid is handmatig in te stellen door het afstelwiel (15) via de instelschroef (11) te draaien. Deze schroef is bereikbaar als de molen in de koffiemachine is geplaatst. Het afstelwiel is voorzien van een maalgrofheidschaal die door een klein venster (12) is af te lezen. Een 24V-motor in de basis drijft de onderste maalschijf aan via een tandwielkast naar de aandrijfas (17). De maalgrofheid aanpassen De maalgrofheid kan zonder de molen uit de koffiemachine te halen, worden aangepast. De werkelijke maalgrofheid is af te lezen in het kleine venster linksonder in de molen. 1. Pas de maalgrofheid aan met de schroef (type Philips), rechtsonder in de basis. ▪ Draai naar links (+) voor een grovere maling / hoger getal. ▪ Draai naar rechts (-) voor een fijnere maling / lager getal. ▪ Draai de schroef in de gewenste richting en bekijk de indicator voor de huidige maalgrofheid. TIP Pas de maalgrofheid aan als de molen draait. Voer bijvoorbeeld een testmaling uit of schenk een recept op basis van bonen. Na aanpassing: voer twee testmalingen uit om zeker te weten dat de molen de koffiebonen met de juiste maalgrofheid bereidt. Stel de maalgrofheid in op 6 (fabrieksinstelling) of op de voorkeurswaarde die al bekend was. Neem een testdrank om de smaak te testen en schrijf ter referentie de definitief ingestelde maalgrofheid op. De buitenste zones van de schaal zijn roodgekleurd (waardes lager dan 1,5 en hoger dan 10,5). Opmerking Stel de maalgrofheid niet in op de rode zones. Malen met een waarde onder 1,5 resulteert in een inconsistente uitgiftehoeveelheid van gemalen koffie. Een waarde hoger dan 10,5 kan verstopping in de molen veroorzaken. BELANGRIJK Een nieuwe molen heeft een zogenaamde inloopperiode nodig. Na ongeveer 1.000 kopjes koffie stelt u de maalgrofheid opnieuw in (zie boven). Dit hoeft maar één keer (of wanneer een nieuwe molen of nieuwe maalschijven worden geplaatst). De brewer verwijderen en plaatsen 1. Om bij de koffiemolen te komen, moet u eerst de container voor koffiebonen verwijderen. ▪ De molen wordt op molenhouders in de basis geplaatst en alleen met de aandrijfas vastgezet. 2. Om de molen te verwijderen, tilt u hem uit de basis in de richting van de pijl. 3. Plaats de molen in de basis en zorg dat de molenuitlaat in de juiste richting wijst. ▪ Draai de schroef van de molen zodat de aandrijfas ‘past’ en helemaal naar beneden gaat. De aandrijfas moet in de motoraandrijving ‘passen’. De koffiemolen schoonmaken Geadviseerd wordt de molen regelmatig (maandelijks) schoon te maken om verstopping door oude, gemalen koffie in het molenhuis te voorkomen. Ook verbrande bonen en ‘vreemde’ voorwerpen (zoals hout en stenen) kunnen de molen blokkeren en moeten worden verwijderd. LET OP Open de molen niet in de koffiemachine. Haal hem eerst uit de machine. Procedure Voer de volgende stappen uit: 1. Verwijder de koffiemolen uit de machine. 2. Open het molenhuis. 3. Reinig de maalschijven en de binnenkant van het molenhuis (vergeet de inkeping rondom de schijven niet). 4. Sluit het molenhuis. 5. Plaats de koffiemolen in de machine. De maalschijven vervangen OPMERKING De maalschijven moeten na het malen van 750 kg koffiebonen worden vervangen. De bovenste en onderste schijven zijn identiek. De schroeven in de onderste en bovenste schijf zijn NIET identiek. Benodigd gereedschap • Philips-schroevendraaier Procedure Voer de volgende stappen uit: 1. Verwijder de koffiemolen uit de machine. 2. Verwijder de molenuitlaat. ▪ Spreid de twee borgclips (1) waarmee de uitlaat aan de molen is bevestigd. ▪ Schuif de uitlaat in de richting van de pijl (2) en neem hem uit de molen. 3. Verwijder het bovenstel van het molenhuis. ▪ Draai de kap van het bovenstel in de richting van de pijl (met de klok mee!) om de bayonetsluiting te openen en verwijder de bovenkant van de koffiemolen. 4. Verwijder de schroeven uit de bovenste maalschijf. 5. Verwijder de bovenste schijf. 6. Zorg dat het montage-oppervlak schoon is, voordat u de nieuwe bovenste maalschijf plaatst. 7. Plaats de bovenste maalschijf. OPMERKING De bovenste en onderste schijven zijn identiek. 8. Bevestig de bovenste schijf met drie schroeven. LET OP Zorg dat u de juiste schroef pakt (zie foto). Draai de schroef voorzichtig maar stevig vast. 9. Draai de drie schroeven in de onderste schijf los en verwijder ze. 10. Verwijder de onderste schijf. 11. Reinig het molenhuis en zorg dat het montageoppervlak voor de onderste maalschijf schoon is (ter voorkoming van een andere maalgrofheid). 12. Plaats de nieuwe, onderste maalschijf. OPMERKING De bovenste en onderste schijven zijn identiek. 13. Bevestig de onderste maalschijf met drie schroeven. LET OP Zorg dat u de juiste schroef pakt (zie foto). Draai de schoef voorzichtig maar stevig vast. 14. Sluit het molenhuis. ▪ Installeer het bovenstel van het molenhuis. ▪ Plaats het bovenstel van het molenhuis bovenop de molen een draai het in de richting van de pijl (tegen de klok in!) om het te sluiten en op het molenhuis vast te zetten. 15. Installeer de molenuitlaat. ▪ Schuif de molenuitlaat in de richting van de pijl op de buitenkant van het molenhuis en zorg ervoor dat de borgclips van de uitlaat goed vastklikken. De D-molen afstellen De D-molen staat af fabriek op de standaard maalgrofheid van 6. Deze waarde komt overeen met de ruimte van ca. 0,25 mm tussen de twee maalschijven. Opnieuw afstellen is mogelijk als deze waarde, die af te lezen is in venstertje op de molen, niet overeenkomt met de werkelijke ruimte tussen de maalschijven. Dit kan gebeuren: • wanneer nieuwe maalschijven zijn geplaatst. • na de eerste inloopperiode van de maalschijven (na het malen van bonen voor 1.000 kopjes koffie). Benodigd gereedschap • Torx schroevendraaier maat 15 Procedure Voer de volgende stappen uit. 1. Verwijder de afstelkap. ▪ Buig de vier borgclips (1) in de richting van de pijp en trek de afstelkap (2) van het molenhuis. 2. Verwijder de schroeven van het afstelwiel. ▪ Trek het afstelwiel uit de aandrijfas in de richting van de pijl. De afstelschijf is nu zichtbaar. 3. Om de afstelschijf te kunnen draaien, steekt u er twee schroeven in en draait u ze een paar keer. 4. Draai de afstelschijf voorzichtig in de richting van de pijl totdat de twee maalschijven elkaar raken. 5. Controleer of de aandrijfas niet meer kan worden gedraaid. ▪ De maalschijven zijn nu gereset en staan op 0 (nul). 6. Verwijder de twee steunschroeven uit de afstelschijf. ▪ Zorg ervoor dat de huidige positie van de aftelschijf niet verandert. 7. Schuif het afstelwiel over de aandrijfas. Het afstelwiel bevat een restrictor (1) die in een sleuf aan de buitenkant van het molenhuis (2) past. De restrictiesleuf beperkt de rotatie van het afstelwiel tot 120º. ▪ Duw het afstelwiel over de as naar beneden en draai het naar rechts totdat de restrictor in de linkerhoek van de sleuf van het molenhuis zit. 8. Een tweede controle: zor

tekst: Startpositie Na dosering van de koffie wordt de brewer geactiveerd. De motor draait met de klok mee tot gesloten positie. Gesloten positie De gedoseerde koffie wordt tussen de boven- en onderzuiger samengeperst. Hierna wordt water via de zuiger door de samengeperste koffie geperst. Het stroomt vervolgens door het filter in de bovenkant en uitlaat van de brewer. De druk van de zuiger op de samengeperste koffie wordt geregeld door de regelbare stroom van de motor. Open positie Als er voldoende water is gedoseerd, draait de brewer tegen de klok in naar de open positie. Restwisser De brewer loopt door, waarbij de onderzuiger naar de bovenste positie beweegt. Nu draait de brewer met de klok mee en wordt de samengeperste koffie van de zuiger in de afvalbak geveegd. Terug naar start Nadat de koffieresten zijn weggeveegd, draait de brewer met de klok mee naar de startpositie. Startpositie De brewer is klaar voor een nieuwe cyclus.

tekst: Dankzij het unieke, gepatenteerde systeem kan de CoEx®-brewer met één systeem koffie en espresso zetten. De druk is voor koffie en espresso verschillend; koffie wordt met een druk van 3 - 4 bar bereid, espresso met een druk van 9 bar. Het volume van een consumptie is eenvoudig te wijzigen in de software-instellingen van de machine. De contactduur tussen het water en het koffiepoeder is een heel belangrijke factor in de prestatie van de brewer en is voor koffie en espresso nagenoeg hetzelfde. De optimale contactduur tussen water en koffie is 15 - 25 seconden. Om deze waarde te bereiken moet het systeem een restrictor gebruiken. Door de combinatie van hogere druk, lagere volume en een gelijke koffiecontactduur moet de uitstroom van espresso veel kleiner zijn dan de uitstroom van koffie. In de volgende afbeeldingen wordt de oplossing voor het maken van deze twee dranken in één systeem weergegeven. 1. Koffietoevoer Wanneer gekozen is voor koffie is de toevoer in het begin laag en wordt de drukschakelaar niet geactiveerd. (Veer is sterk genoeg om de drukschakelaar in de koffiestand te houden). De koffie passeert de eerste restrictor en stroomt dan door de grote koffie-uitlaat. 2. Espressotoevoer Wanner gekozen is voor espresso dan is de toevoer eerst hoog en wordt de drukschakelaar geactiveerd. (Veer is niet sterk genoeg om de drukschakelaar in de koffiestand te houden). De koffie-uitlaat wordt gesloten en de espresso moet door de tweede restrictie worden geperst, waardoor de toevoer wordt beperkt en de druk naar 9 bar wordt verhoogd. Het drukverschil tussen koffie en espresso is alleen van toepassing op B2C-espressomachines. De CoEx® Fresh Brew- machines (zonder papieren filter) hebben geen veer om tussen koffie- of espresso-druk te schakelen. De bovenzuiger heeft een gekleurde stip die verwijst naar de gatmaat/-maten en drukschakelaar. Machinetype Stipkleur Gatmaten B2C espresso Geel 1,5mm/0,3mm Fresh brew papierloos Wit 0,5mm

tekst: De brewer heeft twee zuigers; de bovenzuiger (beter bekend als filterkop) en de onderzuiger. Drie afdichtringen zijn verantwoordelijk voor het afdichten van de drukruimte: twee in de onderzuiger en één in de bovenzuiger. 1. Onderzuiger 2. Afdichtring (onderzuiger) 3. Bovenzuiger / filterkop Heet water komt de cilinder binnen (via de onderzuiger) tussen de twee afdichtringen in de zuiger. De mix van water en koffiepoeder wordt door het gaas in de bovenzuiger gefilterd en verlaat vervolgens de cilinder. De afdichting in de bovenzuiger en de onderzuiger moeten tijdens het brewingproces bestand zijn tegen de druk van heet water (10 bar). De vorm van de u- cupring (3) voorkomt krassen in de cilinder door koffiekorrels. De bovenste afdichtring (2) hoeft niet bestand te zijn tegen hoge druk, maar is slechts een schraapring. tekst: The pressure reducer reduces the water pressure to a stable pressure independent from the inlet pressure from the mains water supply. The required inlet pressure from the water supply is between 1,0 and 6 bar. The pressure reducer is adjusted to an outlet pressure of about 0,8 - 0,9 bar during an espresso cycle. The input and output tube to the reducer must be connected in the right direction, the reducer works incorrectly in the reversed mode. There is an arrow on the side of the reducer indicating the correct water flow direction. The reducer contains a backflow protection. This backflow protection prevents the possibility that water from the machine is flowing back into the main water supply. Procedure to adjust the pressure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the lower plate from the back of the machine. 2. Remove the plug P1 (see inset). ▪ Check the Hot water system (on page 26) inside view for more details. 3. Connect the manometer to the hose. 4. Pull out the knob to unlock the reducer. 5. Select an (double) espresso. 6. Adjust the reducer by turning the knob during the pump cycle of the espresso selection. ▪ The manometer must show 0,8 - 0,9 bar during an espresso cycle. ▪ Turning clockwise => increase output pressure (when seen from above) ▪ Turning counter clockwise => decrease output pressure 7. Lock the reducer by pushing the knob downwards. 8. Disconnect the manometer and insert the plug in the hose. 9. Place the back plate on the machine. 10. Ready.

tekst: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the quantity of the water flowing through the hot water pressure system. Three functions are based on the water flow meter: 1. The water dosages for the consumptions are based on quantity of the pulses generated by the flow meter. 2. During the startup procedure it is detected if water is flowing into the system. If not, the machine will stop working and show the error messages “start-up problem” and “no water connected” 3. The amount of heating of the boiler is, besides the measurement with the temperature probe, also based on the quantity of incoming water. The water flow meter is built in between the pressure reducer and the pumps. It is a small turbine which produces electrical pulses. Each 360º rotation produces 2 pulses in the sensor (Hall element). The pulses are detected by the control system. The tube to the water flow meter must be connected in the correct position; the flow meter cannot detect water in the reverse mode. There is a small arrow on the water flow meter which shows the right direction. The water flow meter is a 1.8 mm type. Each pulse is about 0.8 ml water. tekst: The pumps are generating the pressure and flow of the water. The pumps increase the pressure to the required brewing pressure (between 1.5 and 10 bar). The pump is a vibration pump. The plunger vibrates up and down to build up pressure. The pump is a 24VAC pump, the electrical signal to the pump is a 24V block pulse. The pressure can be adjusted by the electrical signal (pulse-width) to the pump. A longer pulse gives a higher pressure because the plunger is lifted higher. The maximum pulse width is 20. This figure can be set in the service program, individual for every consumption. Because of the high frequency of the pulses this electronic signal cannot be measured with an ordinary volt meter. The pulses for the two pumps run out of phase, so a stable high pressure is offered to brew an espresso. tekst: Temperature/Level sensor The sensor in the pressure boiler is a combined level and temperature probe. The sensor is isolated from the boiler housing with a plastic isolation clamped with two nuts around the stainless steel sensor housing. NOTE If replacement is needed, always replace the complete sensor, including the nuts. Temperature Recommended temperature settings pressure boiler Temperature Value Normal 92 ºC High 102 ºC Low 75 ºC Standby 65 ºC The temperature is detected by a thermistor mounted in the stainless steel housing. The control system is controlling the temperature in the boiler based on the resistance of the thermistor. Resistance of the thermistor Resistance Temperature 6.5 kW 95 ºC 100 kW 25 ºC 126.7 kW 20 ºC Temperature sensor The temperature is adjustable in the service menu (Boiler temperature (see Boiler(s) on page 119)). The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boiler is 92 ºC. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in the boiler will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer. The control system contains safeties and the warning messages are based on the detected value of the temperature sensor: • A too high temperature, too low temperature, shortcut or disconnected sensor is detected by the control system. • Disconnected temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is above 350 kW. • Shortcut temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is below 1 kW. • Unlikely temperature measured, replace temperature sensor(s). Level sensor The water level in the boiler is detected by the temperature/level sensor. The boiler is connected to ground. On the isolated sensor housing a positive signal is applied from the control system. If the water level reaches the sensor, a current will pass through the water to the ground and the control system will detect this.

tekst: Temperature safety / clixon The temperature safety (also known as clixon) protects the heater against overheating if the control system does not switch off the heater. The safety interrupts the current to the heater directly, if the boiler is overheating. The safety is a housing with a bi-metal disc. If the device gets too hot, the bi-metal disc opens a (normally closed contact) switch. Internals of the Temperature safety 1. Switching arm 2. Transfer pin 3. Base 4. Disc retainer 5. Cap 6. Bi-metal Disc After cooling down, the safety switch can be reset by pressing the pin (1) by hand. Temperature Safety values This coffee machine contains one open boiler and one pressure boiler: The open boiler contains two different clixons. • A boil dry safety, positioned on the top lid of the open boiler. This clixon switches off when the temperature is over 110 °C ± 5 °C. • A temperature safety, positioned in the overflow hose of the open boiler. This clixon switches off when the temperature of the overflow water is over 90 °C ± 5 °C. The pressure boiler contains two identical clixons. • They are both positioned on the side of the pressure boiler. They switch off when the temperature is over 110 °C ± 5 °C.

tekst: The CoEx XL brewer cycle This is one complete cycle of the CoEx XL brewer. 1. The CoEx XL brewer is in starting position. The brewer cylinder is locked against the coffee filter to create a brewer chamber. The grinder runs and the ground coffee falls from the grinder outlet into the brewer chamber (1). 2. Two, motor powered, transport lead screws (1) move the piston (2) back and forth. During grinding, coffee dropped in the brewer chamber is pushed towards the end to prevent spillage. This can be useful when a double dosage of ground coffee is selected. 3. When the required dosage is reached, grinding stops. The piston (1), with on top the inlet filter (2) moves inside the cylinder. The ground coffee, is pressed against the rotating coffee filter (3) creating a coffee puck (CP). 4. Hot water is inserted in the brewer cylinder via a small hose (1) connected to the inlet filter and pressed through the coffee puck (CP), through the coffee filter (2) and into the flow regulator (3). 5. The needle (4) inside the flow regulator moves to regulate the flow (pressure and extraction time). 6. At the end of the brewing cycle, the needle is moved to the ‘aerate’ position to allow the coffee outlet to empty. 7. The piston (1) moves back and connects to the brewer cylinder using the clutches (2) and (3) and pulls the brewer cylinder away from the coffee filter. 8. The piston (1) moves forward again, disconnects all clutches and leaves the brewer cylinder in the same position. The used coffee puck is pushed out of the cylinder. The coffee puck wiper (2) moves the coffee to the waste bucket and cleans the surface of the inlet filter from coffee residue. 9. The piston (1) moves forward completely and pushes the brewing cylinder (2) against the coffee filter (3) where it remains locked. 10. The needle (4) moves to the ‘flush’ position to redirect any remaining output to the drain outlet. 11. The piston returns to the start position and is ready for the next brew. 12. The needle in the flow regulator returns to the starting position.

titel: Replace service parts in the brewer
tekst: WARNING Only loosen silver-colored screws in the brewer mentioned in this manual. All other screws (black-colored) are adjusted and secured in the factory and should NOT be loosened/removed as this will void the guarantee. The only serviceable parts in the brewer that need to be replaced after 50.000 brewing cycles (or 2 years) are: 1. the coffee filter assembly with seals. 2. the inner cylinder. 3. the inlet filter assembly with seals. A complete set is available as spare part set. NOTE Replace all parts in one session. The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water resistant label on top of the brewer gear box) contains the manufacturing date. The number format is year-week-sequence number. Procedure Follow the steps to replace the service parts. 1. Before removing the brewer from the machine, first place the brewer in the Service position. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this, check the section Place brewer in service position (on page 65). 2. Remove the brewer from the machine and remove the cover from the brewer. Check the chapter 'Remove and clean the brewer' in the User manual for details. Remove inlet filter Follow this procedure: 1. Remove one screw (1) that secures the inlet filter. (M4/ Length=16mm) 2. Turn the inlet filter clockwise (2) to release the bayonet locking. 3. Loosen and remove the inlet filter from the piston. Remove inner cylinder Follow this procedure: 1. Remove 1 screw that secures the inner cylinder. (M4/ Length=16mm). 2. Turn the brewer around again. 3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) and remove it from the brewer. Replace coffee filter Follow this procedure: 1. Push the cylinder down by hand. 2. If the cylinder is locked, locate the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Pull the right clutch up (or push from the back) and, at the same time, push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to access the coffee filter. 3. Place the brewer in vertical position with the brewer locking grip facing upwards. 4. Locate the 2 screws in between the gears. Loosen and remove the 2 screws. (3.5/Length=8mm) WARNING Do NOT unfasten any of the black-colored screws to avoid warranty issues. Silver-colored screws can be disassembled for service part replacement. 5. Remove the old coffee filter. 6. Place the new coffee filter. ▪ Make sure that the (coffee) water connectors are in line with each other ▪ When needed, turn the coffee filter slightly to fit the square filter shaft into the drive gear. 7. Secure the coffee filter with 2 screws. WARNING Make sure the same 3.5x8 Philips head screws are used. Install inner cylinder Follow this procedure: 1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter. 2. Lower the inner cylinder inside the brewer and tilt it around the piston. 3. Slide it inside the outer cylinder. 4. Turn the brewer upside down. Secure the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16). Install inlet filter Follow this procedure: 1. Position the new inlet filter. ▪ Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1). ▪ Lower the filter on the bayonet locking (inset 2) and turn the filter to lock. ▪ Secure the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/ Length=16mm) 2. Finished, the service parts are installed. 3. Place the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

tekst: The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer house. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures a correct mixing of the ingredient(s) and water. By the rotation of the mixer propeller, air is mixed with the water and ingredient(s) and a foam layer is formed. This will improve the taste and the appearance of the consumption. tekst: General The D-grinder uses high performance grinder discs that give a consistent grind and operates at about twice the speed of the Schaerer grinder to grind beans for coffee and espresso. This means that the same amount of ground coffee is created in half the time. Check the specifications at the end of this chapter for more details. The D-grinder is easy to clean and settings (like grinding degree) are maintained when the grinder is opened for cleaning. The grinding degree of the D-grinder is not measured in pins and teeth but displayed in an indicator window on the grinder. The indicator shows a scale from 0 to 12 (actual degrees divided by 10). The D-grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 6 in the factory. Note that the type of beans used and (local) flavor expectations may require a different setting of the grinder in the coffee machine. NOTE Existing coffee related recipes/configurations need to be changed if they are used for the D-grinder but made for the Schaerer grinder (because of the higher output of ground coffee). 1. Auger 10. Grinder motor drive 11. Grinding degree adjustment 2. Grinder house top assembly screw 3. Upper grinding disc (stationary) 12. Grinding degree scale window 4. Screws upper grinding disc 13. Grinder adjustment cover 5. Screws lower grinding disc 14. Screws worm wheel assembly 6. Lower grinding disc (rotating) 15. Adjustment wheel 7. Grinder base / Motor cover 16. Grinder outlet 8. Grinder stand 17. Drive shaft 9. Grinder house 18. Grinding disc assembly bottom The grinder unit consists of the top assembly (2) that contains the stationary –non moving- upper grinding disc (3). The top assembly is secured to the grinder house using a bayonet catch for easy access. The grinder house (9) contains the bottom assembly with the rotating lower grinding disc (6). By adjusting the lower grinding disc up and down, the air gap between the two grinder discs can be set very accurately. The gap between the two grinder discs determines the grain size of the ground coffee also known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree is set manually by rotating the adjustment wheel (15) with an adjustment screw (11). This screw is accessible when the grinder is installed in the coffee machine. The adjustment wheel contains a grinding degree scale that is visible through a small window (12). A 24-volt motor in the grinder base powers the lower grinding disc via a gear box to the drive shaft (17). Change the grinding degree The grinding degree can be adjusted without removing the grinder from the coffee machine. The actual grinding degree is visible in a small indicator window in the bottom left of the grinder. 1. Adjust the grinding degree with the (Philips type) screw, accessible on the bottom right of the grinder base. ▪ Turn left (+) for a coarser grinding / higher number. ▪ Turn right (-) for a finer grinding / lower number. ▪ Turn the screw in the desired direction and check the indicator to see the current grinding degree. TIP Change the grinding degree when the grinder is running. For instance, run a test grind or dispense a beans-based recipe. After adjustment: first run two test grinds to be sure that the grinder will dispense the ground coffee with the correct grinding degree. Set the grinding degree to the value 6 (factory default) or to the preferred value that was already known. Take a test beverage to test for taste and write down the finally set grinding degree for future reference. The outer areas of the scale are marked in red (values lower than 1.5 and higher than 10.5). NOTE Do not set the grinding degree in the red areas. Grinding with a value below 1.5 will result in an inconsistent dispense quantity of ground coffee. A value higher than 10.5 can clog the grinder. IMPORTANT A new grinder needs a so-called break-in period. After about 1000 cups of coffee, set the grinding degree again (see above). This is only needed once (or when installing a new grinder or new grinder discs). Remove and place the grinder 1. To access the grinder, first remove the bean canister. ▪ The grinder is placed and positioned on grinder stands inside the grinder base and is secured only using the driving shaft. 2. To remove the grinder, lift it from the grinder base in the direction of the arrow. 3. Place the grinder in the grinder base and make sure the grinder outlet points in the right direction. ▪ Rotate the grinder auger to allow the drive shaft to ‘fit’ and move down completely. The drive shaft must ‘fit’ in the motor drive. Clean the grinder Regular (monthly) cleaning of the grinder is recommended to prevent clogging of old ground coffee inside the grinder house. Also, burned beans and ‘foreign’ objects (like wood or stones) can block the grinder and need to be removed. CAUTION Do not open the grinder inside the coffee machine. First remove it from the machine. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the grinder from the machine. 2. Open the grinder house. 3. Clean the grinder discs and the inside of the grinder house (do not forget to clean the gap around the discs). 4. Close the grinder house. 5. Install the grinder in the machine. Replace the grinder discs NOTE The grinding discs need to be replaced after grinding 750 kg of coffee beans. The upper and lower discs are identical. The screws in the lower and the upper disc are NOT identical. Required tools • Philips screwdriver Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the grinder from the machine. 2. Remove the grinder outlet. ▪ spread the two fixation clips (1) that secure the outlet to the grinder. ▪ slide the outlet in the direction of the arrow (2) and remove it from the grinder. 3. Remove the grinder house top assembly. ▪ Turn the cover of the top assembly in the direction of the arrow (clockwise!) to unlock the bayonet catch and remove the top assembly from the grinder. 4. Remove screws from upper grinding disc. 5. Remove the upper disc. 6. Before placing the new upper grinding disc make sure that the mounting surface is clean. 7. Place the upper grinder disc. NOTE The upper and lower discs are identical. 8. Secure the upper disc with three screws. CAUTION Make sure to pick the correct screw (see picture). Tighten the screws gently, but firmly. 9. Loosen and remove the three screws in the lower disc. 10. Remove the lower disc. 11. Clean up the grinder house and make sure that the mounting surface for the lower grinding disc is clean (to prevent a different grinding degree). 12. Place the new lower grinding disc. NOTE The upper and lower discs are identical. 13. Secure the lower grinding disc with three screws. CAUTION Make sure to pick the correct screw (see picture). Tighten the screws gently, but firmly. 14. Close the grinder house. ▪ Install grinder house top assembly. ▪ Place the grinder house top assembly on top of the grinder and turn it in the direction of the arrow (counter clockwise!) to close and lock it to the grinder house. 15. Install grinder outlet. ▪ Slide the grinder outlet in the direction of the arrow on the outside of the grinder house and make sure the locking clips of the outlet lock properly. Readjust the D-grinder The D-grinder has been set in the factory to the default grinding degree of 6, this number corresponds to a gap between the two grinder discs of about 0.25 mm. Readjustment is possible if this number, shown in the little window on the grinder, does not match with the actual gap between the grinder discs. This can happen : • when new grinder discs are installed. • after the initial break-in period of the grinder discs (after grinding beans for 1000 cups of coffee). Required tools • Torx 15 screwdriver Procedure Perform the following steps 1. Remove the adjustment cover. ▪ Bend the four locking clips (1) in the direction of the arrows and pull the adjustment cover (2) from the grinder house. 2. Remove the screws that secure the adjustment wheel. ▪ Pull the adjustment wheel from the drive shaft in the direction of the arrow. The adjustment disc is now visible. 3. To be able to turn the adjustment disc, insert two screws and give them a few turns. 4. Turn the adjustment disc gently in the direction of the arrow until the two grinding discs touch each other. 5. Check that the drive shaft cannot be turned anymore. ▪ The grinder discs are now reset to 0 (zero). 6. Remove the two support screws from the adjustment disc. ▪ Make sure not to change the current position of the adjustment disc. 7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º. ▪ Push the adjustment wheel down the shaft and turn it clockwise until the restrictor is in the left corner of the slot of the grinder house. 8. A second check: make sure that the number 0 of the scale on the adjustment wheel is positioned above the small vertical mark in the outside of the grinder

If no consumptions are made, the temperature in pressure boiler 2 will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer. The control system contains safeties and the warning messages are based on the detected value of the temperature sensor: • A too high temperature, too low temperature, shortcut or disconnected sensor is detected by the control system. • Disconnected temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is above 350 kW. • Shortcut temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is below 1 kW. • Unlikely temperature measured, replace temperature sensor(s). Level sensor The water level in the boiler is detected by the temperature/level sensor. The boiler is connected to ground. On the isolated sensor housing a positive signal is applied from the control system. If the water level reaches the sensor, a current will pass through the water to the ground and the control system will detect this.

tekst: The fresh milk system takes the chilled fresh milk from the refrigerator and adds steam to produce warm milk. Air can be added to create a foamy milk topping. The fresh milk system consists of the following components: • Steam boiler • Air pump • Air regulator • Fresh milk pump with cabinet • Fresh milk frother system A machine with a fresh milk system is equipped with a hot water system with a pressure boiler (boiler #2) and a steam boiler (boiler #1). A schematic overview can be found in chapter Schematic diagram of the water system (on page 26). The fresh milk process is visualized with the following timeline: Milk pump full speed Milk pump set speed Steam valve open 0,2 Air pump (optional) 0,2 The milk pump runs shortly at full speed in order to fill up the milk tube until the milk reaches the frother inlet. Then the following starts simultaneously: • The milk pump starts pumping milk again at a set speed. • The steam valve opens. • The air pump starts pumping air (optional for adding foam bubbles). Inside the frother, chilled milk is heated up by the steam and optionally mixed with air. When the desired quantity of fresh milk topping is reached the milk pump stops pumping. To prevent splashing of milk the air pump stops 0,2 seconds before the milk pump stops. And to clear the frother from any milk remains, the steam valve will close 0,2 seconds after the milk pump stops. A standard recipe routine at the end of each fresh milk cycle is the reverse pumping of the milk pump (not visualized in the timeline). This will transport the remaining milk from the milk tube back into the milk container. At the end the milk pump is given a short pulse forward, which creates a syphon effect that will level the milk in the tube with the milk in the container. The pump sounds are clearly audible in the machine at the end of a fresh milk cycle.

tekst: Inside the frother, chilled milk is heated up by the steam (and the optional air). The steam and optionally air enters the first chamber (1) through the nozzle (A). The milk is added to the first chamber from the side (B). Inside the second chamber (2), steam condenses and heats up the milk. The warm, and optionally frothed milk flows out of the chamber holes. Finally, the milk escapes through the outlet (C).

tekst: Fresh Milk recipe parameters In a fresh milk recipe you can adjust the following parameters: • Milk pump full speed (duration): Period of time in which milk is delivered at 100% pump speed. This determines the amount of milk that initially fills up the milk tube until it reaches the frother inlet. This value is used for all fresh milk recipes. • Milk pump speed: Amount of milk per unit of time. This determines the milk temperature. • Milk pump duration: Period of time in which milk is delivered to the frother. This determines the milk quantity. • Steam valve duration: Period of time in which steam is delivered to the frother. • Air pump duration: Period of time in which air is delivered to the frother. The steam valve duration and air pump duration are normally set longer than the milk pump duration. Both both stop automatically for correct working. Furthermore, the air flow can be manually adjusted with a screwdriver. This reduces or increases the amount of added air in the milk. Setting up the Fresh Milk system The desired fresh milk addition or topping is achieved by adjusting the fresh milk recipes, explained in the next paragraph. However, before you can start adjusting recipes you need to set up the fresh milk system correctly. Setting up the fresh milk system is done by testing and adjusting the Hot Milk FM recipe. The following procedure describes in detail how to do the setup. If any problems occur consult the troubleshooting guide fresh milk in Troubleshooting guide Fresh Milk (on page 53). • Check if the chilled milk is UHT processed and still fresh. Only use UHT milk! And preferably whole milk. • Check if the chilled milk has a temperature between + 4 °C and + 6 °C. • Check if the fresh milk components (frother and tubes) are clean. • Check if the milk tube with restriction is placed in the chilled milk. • Check if the screen displays any warnings or failures that need to be resolved first. 1. Log in into the service menu and check if the steam boiler temperature is set at 129 ºC. Check if the actual temperature is close to this setting. 2. Make sure the machine is heated up properly by taking a couple of test consumptions without milk. 3. Take a test cup by selecting a Hot Milk FM Test consumption: ▪ In the service menu go to Recipe settings -> Water/ ingredients settings -> Hot Milk FM -> Test. 4. Place a temperature gauge and read out the temperature of the milk. ▪ The temperature should be between 65 ºC and 70 ºC. 5. If the temperature needs to be adjusted, go to Recipe settings -> Water/ingredients settings -> Hot Milk FM -> milk pump -> [Speed] and adjust the milk pump speed: ▪ Increase the speed for a lower milk temperature. ▪ Decrease the speed for a higher milk temperature. NOTE The default milk pump speed is 50%. Try to keep the speed above 45% for proper functioning (this also depends on the type of milk and actual steam temperature). 6. Take a Hot Milk FM test cup to check the result. Repeat the previous step and adjust the speed until you have the correct temperature. ▪ The final pump speed setting is also applicable for the other fresh milk recipes, see the next paragraph (Adjusting fresh milk recipes). 7. Check the amount of milk in the cup. If the quantity is correct continue with step 9. 8. Adjust the milk pump duration: ▪ Increase the duration for more milk. ▪ Decrease the duration for less milk. 9. Take a test cup to check the result. ▪ Keep adjusting the milk pump duration and taking Hot Milk FM test cups until you have the correct amount of milk. 10. If the foam layer is correct continue with step 14. 11. Open the front door of the machine. 12. Locate the air regulator adjustment screw, see picture. 13. Adjust the air regulator with a screwdriver (flat blade): ▪ Turn right - less air / less and smaller foam bubbles. ▪ Turn left - more air / more and larger foam bubbles. ▪ The factory setting is 1½ strokes open. This is almost fully open. 14. Take a test cup again. Keep adjusting the air regulator and taking Hot Milk FM test cups until you have the correct amount of air. 15. Close the front door, log out of the service menu and return to the user menu. 16. The setup of the fresh milk system is now complete. Adjusting fresh milk recipes • After a correct setup (see previous paragraph) you can start adjusting the fresh milk recipes to your needs. The parameters Milk pump full speed and Milk pump speed from the Hot Milk FM setup procedure are reused here. You can change the milk duration parameter to increase or decrease the amount of milk. In the following table, the fresh milk recipes and their relevant factory settings are listed: Recipe Sub-recipe Milk pump Milk pump Milk pump Steam Air pump full speed set speed duration duration duration (1) (1) Chocomilk FM sub chocomilk FM 3.0 50 7.0 7.2 6.8 Cappuccino FM sub cappuccino FM 3.0 50 15.0 15.2 14.8 Café au lait FM sub café au lait FM 3.0 50 9.0 n/a n/a Macchiato FM sub macchiato FM 3.0 50 10.0 10.2 9.8 Hot Milk FM n/a 3.0 50 18.0 18.2 17.8 Cold Milk FM n/a 15.0 n/a n/a 0.5 n/a (1) Steam duration and air pump duration are handled automatically where needed. If any problems occur, run the setup procedure again or consult the troubleshooting guide fresh milk in the following paragraph.

tekst: If any problems occur, run the setup procedure again or consult this troubleshooting guide fresh milk. Milk temperature too high Possible causes are: 1. Milk temperature too low Possible causes are: 1. Temperature of the incoming chilled milk is too low. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 2. Pressure and temperature drop due to triggered clixon. ▪ Check if any boiler clixons have been triggered and reconnect the clixon(s) if necessary. 3. Temperature of the steam boiler is too low. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 4. Milk pump speed is too high. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 5. The machine has not warmed up yet (e.g. when the machine has not been used for a while). ▪ Take a number of test consumptions and check if the temperature increases. 6. The milk pump full speed duration is too long, the milk tube is flooded and chilled milk passes the frother before frothing takes place. ▪ Decrease the milk pump full speed duration. The factory setting is 3.8 seconds. ▪ Check if the milk inlet restrictor is inserted in the hose (the hose end in the milk container), check the section Milk pump (on page 48) for details. Milk temperature varies Possible causes are: 1. The pressure reducer after the inlet valve is not set properly. Too much cold water enters the boiler and results in a pressure and temperature drop. ▪ Adjust the pressure reducer to the correct setting, see. Too much milk Possible causes are: 1. Milk pump duration is too long. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 2. Milk pump speed is too high. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 3. Milk tube restriction is missing. ▪ Place a restriction (5MVL215) at the inlet of the milk tube. Not enough milk Possible causes are: 1. Milk pump duration is too short. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 2. Milk pump speed is too low. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 3. Milk system is not cleaned properly. ▪ Check the fresh milk components for clogged up milk. ▪ Check if the milk has gone bad and needs to be replaced. ▪ Clean or replace the fresh milk components (see user manual). No milk Possible causes are: 1. Milk container is empty. ▪ Refill or replace milk container. 2. Milk system is not cleaned properly. ▪ Check the fresh milk components for clogged up milk. ▪ Check if the milk has gone bad and needs to be replaced. ▪ Clean or replace the fresh milk components (see user manual). 3. Milk pump is not active during recipe. ▪ Check if fresh milk is included in the (sub)recipe. ▪ Check if the milk pump duration is at least 5 seconds. ▪ Test the output by running a milk pump test from the service menu. ▪ Check the wiring of the milk pump. 4. Milk pump stalls. ▪ Increase the milk pump speed (should be at least 45). Continue with step 7 (Check the amount of milk in the cup) of the setup procedure in order to compensate the recipe durations. Foam bubbles are too large Possible causes are: 1. Too much air is added. ▪ Adjust the air regulator clockwise with a screwdriver to decrease the air quantity. ▪ Check also the setup procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. Not enough foam bubbles Possible causes are: 1. Not enough air is added. ▪ Turn the air regulator left with a screwdriver to increase the air quantity. ▪ Check also the setup procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. 2. Milk in the milk container is not UHT processed. ▪ Refill or replace milk container with UHT processed milk. 3. Milk temperature is too high. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. No foam bubbles Possible causes are: 1. Air is not reaching the frother. ▪ Check if the air pump is included in the (sub)recipe. ▪ Test the output of the air pump by running an air pump test from the service menu. ▪ Turn the air regulator left with a screwdriver to increase the air quantity. ▪ Check also the setup procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. Splashing milk Possible causes are: 1. Milk system is not cleaned properly. ▪ Check the fresh milk components for clogged up milk. ▪ Check if the milk has gone bad and needs to be replaced. ▪ Clean or replace the fresh milk components (see user manual). ▪ Air regulator opened too far. First close the air regulator by turning fully clockwise and then re-adjust. 2. Milk pump speed is too low. ▪ Follow the setup procedure and then the adjustment procedure described in the Fresh Milk recipes (on page 50) chapter. Large amount of steam from the outlet Possible causes are: before the milk starts coming out 1. The milk pump full speed duration is too short. Thus the chilled milk has not yet reached the frother inlet when frothing is started. ▪ Increase the milk pump full speed duration. Factory setting is 3.0 seconds.

tekst: By adjusting the upper grinder blade axially, the air gap between the two grinder blades can be set very accurately. This air gap defines the grain size of the ground coffee, what is known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree setting is made manually on a worm gear. The powder (ground coffee) is discharged into the powder outlet through four cams attached evenly around the circumference of the star shaft. 1. Grinder housing 2. Star shaft 3. Lower grinder disc 4. Upper grinder disc 5. Upper part of grinder 6. Grinding degree disc (setting scale) 7. n/a for Nio 8. Powder outlet 9. Coffee beans 10. Ground coffee (coffee powder) 11. Motor / gear 12. Rubber / metal buffer 13. Visual check during service Changing the grinding degree The grinder disc contains grinding degree numbers from 0 to 5. The grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 1.5 (S=Standard model) or 2 (XG=XG model using advanced grinder discs) during production. However, the type of coffee beans used and (local) flavor expectations will probably be different. Adjust the grinding degree for the best ground coffee and ‘fine-tune’ for the best flavor coffee and espresso. The grinder needs to be removed from the machine to change the grinding degree. A fixation spring is used to secure the grinding disc to a specific grinding degree. 1. Remove the fixation spring. ▪ Bend the teeth away from the grinding disc and lift the spring. 2. Rotate the grinding disc to change the grinder degree. ▪ Set it 0.5 lower for a finer grinding. ▪ Set it 0.5 higher for a more coarse-grained coffee. 3. Insert the fixation spring. NOTE After adjusting the grinder, first take two consumptions to get rid of the old coffee in the grinder chute. After these two consumptions, check the new grinder setting with taking a test consumption, checking crème layer, taste etc.

If the device gets too hot, the bi-metal disc opens a (normally closed contact) switch. Internals of the Temperature safety 1. Switching arm 2. Transfer pin 3. Base 4. Disc retainer 5. Cap 6. Bi-metal Disc After cooling down, the safety switch can be reset by pressing the pin (1) by hand. This clixon switches off when the temperature is over 110 °C ± 5 °C. • A temperature safety, positioned in the overflow hose of the open boiler. This clixon switches off when the temperature of the overflow water is over 90 °C ± 5 °C.

tekst: 1. Brewer chamber 2. Transport wheels 3. Brewer outlet 4. Piston 5. Cylinder The brewer operates according to the vacuum principle. Ground coffee is dosed into the brewer chamber, together with the hot water. At that moment the brewer is in the rest mode (A). Then the brewer motor turns, moving the piston up (B). This movement mixes the water and the coffee mixed, improving the extraction. Consequently, less ground coffee is necessary to obtain stronger and more tasteful coffee. Subsequently, the piston moves down, pulling the coffee through the filter paper (C). The coffee flows out of the cylinder through the outlet into the cup. The filter paper together with the coffee residue is transported by means of the transport wheels, when the piston is in the almost lower position and the brewer chamber is lifted. After this, the brewer returns to the rest mode (D) and is ready for the next cycle.

tekst: Readjusting the clamp fore is necessary when too much water leaks between the brewer and the brewer chamber. This is the case when the filter paper becomes wet, more the 10 mm around the brewer chamber. Nevertheless, when the clamp force is adjusted to high, excessive wear can occur or the brewer motor can get stuck. Adjust the brewer chamber clamp force as follows: 1. Open the machine door. 2. Tear the filter paper in front of the brewer and behind the brewer. 3. Remove the brewer from the machine. 4. Turn the brewer piston up using the Uni-key until the brewer chamber flips over. 5. Remove the filter paper from the brewer. Place a new piece of filter paper between the brewer and the brewer chamber. 6. Move the brewer piston in the upper position (connecting rods in line). 7. Turn the adjustment nut on top of the H-frame clockwise, until filter paper is just clamped between brewer and brewer chamber. The brewer chamber may not be pushed onto the brewer during the adjustment. 8. Turn the nut ½ - 1 turn clockwise. NOTE It should be possible to move the brewer chamber slightly in the closed position. 9. Place the brewer in the machine 10. Place the filter paper according to the procedure in the user’s manual. 11. Check the operation of the brewer by selecting a coffee consumption. Take notice of the following things: When the brewer chamber clamp force is set too low, water is leaking between the brewer and the brewer chamber. Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn clockwise. The clamp force is set too high when the brewer piston does not move smoothly in the down position (during lifting of the brewer chamber). Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn counter-clockwise. Check operation of the brewer again. 12. Close the machine door.

tekst: To prevent that old coffee remains in the brewer chamber, during the transportation of the filter paper, the distance between the layers of coffee residue can be adjusted. Especially for large dosing quantities of coffee this can be necessary. Nevertheless the distance between the layers should not be adjusted too big, to prevent unnecessary loss of paper (more often replacement of the paper reel). NOTE Always check and/or readjust the brewer chamber clamp force first, before adjusting the paper transport. Changing the clamp force will influence the paper transport. The paper transport is adjusted correct when: After transport of the filter paper, no coffee remains in the brewer chamber. The distance between the layers of coffee residue is between 5 – 10 mm. Adjust the paper transport as follows: 1. Hold the adjustment bolt and loosen the lock nut. 2. Turn the adjustment bolt counter-clockwise when coffee residue remains in the brewer chamber / Turn the adjustment bolt clockwise when the distance between the layers of coffee residue is too big. 3. Tighten the lock nut. 4. Check the operation of the paper transport. 5. Check the distance between the layers of coffee residue. NOTE The adjustment bolt can be easily turned while the brewer chamber is lifted. 6. Place the service key in the door switch. The machine is switched on now. NOTE When the machine is switched on, you should take the utmost care when performing the functions through the internal service panel. 7. Take at least 4x consumptions to test the paper transport distance. 8. Check the functioning of the machine by taking a test drink (coffee). Place a cup or a jug underneath the nozzle to collect the hot test drink.

tekst: General The D-grinder uses high performance grinder discs that give a consistent grind and operates at about twice the speed of the Schaerer grinder to grind beans for coffee and espresso. This means that the same amount of ground coffee is created in half the time. Check the specifications at the end of this chapter for more details. The D-grinder is easy to clean and settings (like grinding degree) are maintained when the grinder is opened for cleaning. The grinding degree of the D-grinder is not measured in pins and teeth but displayed in an indicator window on the grinder. The indicator shows a scale from 0 to 12 (actual degrees divided by 10). The D-grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 6 in the factory. Note that the type of beans used and (local) flavor expectations may require a different setting of the grinder in the coffee machine. NOTE Existing coffee related recipes/configurations need to be changed if they are used for the D-grinder but made for the Schaerer grinder (because of the higher output of ground coffee). 1. Auger 10. Grinder motor drive 11. Grinding degree adjustment 2. Grinder house top assembly screw 3. Upper grinding disc (stationary) 12. Grinding degree scale window 4. Screws upper grinding disc 13. Grinder adjustment cover 5. Screws lower grinding disc 14. Screws worm wheel assembly 6. Lower grinding disc (rotating) 15. Adjustment wheel 7. Grinder base / Motor cover 16. Grinder outlet 8. Grinder stand 17. Drive shaft 9. Grinder house 18. Grinding disc assembly bottom The grinder unit consists of the top assembly (2) that contains the stationary –non moving- upper grinding disc (3). The top assembly is secured to the grinder house using a bayonet catch for easy access. The grinder house (9) contains the bottom assembly with the rotating lower grinding disc (6). By adjusting the lower grinding disc up and down, the air gap between the two grinder discs can be set very accurately. The gap between the two grinder discs determines the grain size of the ground coffee also known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree is set manually by rotating the adjustment wheel (15) with an adjustment screw (11). This screw is accessible when the grinder is installed in the coffee machine. The adjustment wheel contains a grinding degree scale that is visible through a small window (12). A 24-volt motor in the grinder base powers the lower grinding disc via a gear box to the drive shaft (17). Change the grinding degree The grinding degree can be adjusted without removing the grinder from the coffee machine. The actual grinding degree is visible in a small indicator window in the bottom left of the grinder. 1. Adjust the grinding degree with the (Philips type) screw, accessible on the bottom right of the grinder base. ▪ Turn left (+) for a coarser grinding / higher number. ▪ Turn right (-) for a finer grinding / lower number. ▪ Turn the screw in the desired direction and check the indicator to see the current grinding degree. TIP Change the grinding degree when the grinder is running. For instance, run a test grind or dispense a beans-based recipe. After adjustment: first run two test grinds to be sure that the grinder will dispense the ground coffee with the correct grinding degree. Set the grinding degree to the value 6 (factory default) or to the preferred value that was already known. Take a test beverage to test for taste and write down the finally set grinding degree for future reference. The outer areas of the scale are marked in red (values lower than 1.5 and higher than 10.5). NOTE Do not set the grinding degree in the red areas. Grinding with a value below 1.5 will result in an inconsistent dispense quantity of ground coffee. A value higher than 10.5 can clog the grinder. IMPORTANT A new grinder needs a so-called break-in period. After about 1000 cups of coffee, set the grinding degree again (see above). This is only needed once (or when installing a new grinder or new grinder discs). Remove and place the grinder 1. To access the grinder, first remove the bean canister. ▪ The grinder is placed and positioned on grinder stands inside the grinder base and is secured only using the driving shaft. 2. To remove the grinder, lift it from the grinder base in the direction of the arrow. 3. Place the grinder in the grinder base and make sure the grinder outlet points in the right direction. ▪ Rotate the grinder auger to allow the drive shaft to ‘fit’ and move down completely. The drive shaft must ‘fit’ in the motor drive. Clean the grinder Regular (monthly) cleaning of the grinder is recommended to prevent clogging of old ground coffee inside the grinder house. Also, burned beans and ‘foreign’ objects (like wood or stones) can block the grinder and need to be removed. CAUTION Do not open the grinder inside the coffee machine. First remove it from the machine. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the grinder from the machine. 2. Open the grinder house. 3. Clean the grinder discs and the inside of the grinder house (do not forget to clean the gap around the discs). 4. Close the grinder house. 5. Install the grinder in the machine. Replace the grinder discs NOTE The grinding discs need to be replaced after grinding 750 kg of coffee beans. The upper and lower discs are identical. The screws in the lower and the upper disc are NOT identical. Required tools • Philips screwdriver Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the grinder from the machine. 2. Remove the grinder outlet. ▪ spread the two fixation clips (1) that secure the outlet to the grinder. ▪ slide the outlet in the direction of the arrow (2) and remove it from the grinder. 3. Remove the grinder house top assembly. ▪ Turn the cover of the top assembly in the direction of the arrow (clockwise!) to unlock the bayonet catch and remove the top assembly from the grinder. 4. Remove screws from upper grinding disc. 5. Remove the upper disc. 6. Before placing the new upper grinding disc make sure that the mounting surface is clean. 7. Place the upper grinder disc. NOTE The upper and lower discs are identical. 8. Secure the upper disc with three screws. CAUTION Make sure to pick the correct screw (see picture). Tighten the screws gently, but firmly. 9. Loosen and remove the three screws in the lower disc. 10. Remove the lower disc. 11. Clean up the grinder house and make sure that the mounting surface for the lower grinding disc is clean (to prevent a different grinding degree). 12. Place the new lower grinding disc. NOTE The upper and lower discs are identical. 13. Secure the lower grinding disc with three screws. CAUTION Make sure to pick the correct screw (see picture). Tighten the screws gently, but firmly. 14. Close the grinder house. ▪ Install grinder house top assembly. ▪ Place the grinder house top assembly on top of the grinder and turn it in the direction of the arrow (counter clockwise!) to close and lock it to the grinder house. 15. Install grinder outlet. ▪ Slide the grinder outlet in the direction of the arrow on the outside of the grinder house and make sure the locking clips of the outlet lock properly. Readjust the D-grinder The D-grinder has been set in the factory to the default grinding degree of 6, this number corresponds to a gap between the two grinder discs of about 0.25 mm. Readjustment is possible if this number, shown in the little window on the grinder, does not match with the actual gap between the grinder discs. This can happen : • when new grinder discs are installed. • after the initial break-in period of the grinder discs (after grinding beans for 1000 cups of coffee). Required tools • Torx 15 screwdriver Procedure Perform the following steps 1. Remove the adjustment cover. ▪ Bend the four locking clips (1) in the direction of the arrows and pull the adjustment cover (2) from the grinder house. 2. Remove the screws that secure the adjustment wheel. ▪ Pull the adjustment wheel from the drive shaft in the direction of the arrow. The adjustment disc is now visible. 3. To be able to turn the adjustment disc, insert two screws and give them a few turns. 4. Turn the adjustment disc gently in the direction of the arrow until the two grinding discs touch each other. 5. Check that the drive shaft cannot be turned anymore. ▪ The grinder discs are now reset to 0 (zero). 6. Remove the two support screws from the adjustment disc. ▪ Make sure not to change the current position of the adjustment disc. 7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º. ▪ Push the adjustment wheel down the shaft and turn it clockwise until the restrictor is in the left corner of the slot of the grinder house. 8. A second check: make sure that the number 0 of the scale on the adjustment wheel is positioned above the small vertical mark in the outside of the grinder

tekst: Sensoren De open boiler heeft twee gescheiden sensoren; een niveausensor en een temperatuursensor. De sensoren zijn van de boilerbehuizing gescheiden door kunststof isolatie dat met twee moeren rond de roestvrijstalen sensorbehuizing is geklemd. OPMERKING Gebruik voor elke sensor de juiste isolatie (stopfitting). Zie de handleidingen voor reserveonderdelen voor het correcte onderdeelnummer. OPMERKING Als de sensor moet worden vervangen, vervang deze dan helemaal, inclusief de moeren. Temperatuur- en niveausensoren open boiler 1. Niveausensor 2. Temperatuursensor Temperatuur Aanbevolen temperatuurinstellingen open boiler Temperatuur Waarde Normaal 91 ºC Hoog 98 ºC Laag 70 ºC Stand-by 65 ºC De temperatuur wordt door een thermistor gedetecteerd. Deze is in de roestvrijstalen behuizing gemonteerd. Het regelsysteem regelt de temperatuur in de boiler op basis van de weerstand van de thermistor. Weerstand van de thermistor Weerstand Temperatuur 6,5 kW 95 ºC 100 kW 25 ºC 126,7 kW 20 ºC Temperatuursensor De temperatuur kan in het servicemenu worden aangepast. De optimale temperatuurinstelling is 91 ºC. Het regelsysteem bevat verschillende beveiligingen en toont waarschuwingen gebaseerd op de gedetecteerde waarde van de temperatuursensor: • Een te hoge temperatuur, een te lage temperatuur, kortsluiting of uitgeschakelde sensor • Een sensor wordt uitgeschakeld als de weerstand boven de 350 kW komt. • Kortsluiting temperatuursensor wordt gegenereerd als de weerstand lager is dan 1 kW. Niveausensor Het niveau in de boiler wordt door de roestvrijstalen behuizing van de niveausensor gemeten. De boiler is geaard. Vanuit het regelsysteem wordt een positief signaal op de sensorbehuizing toegepast. Wanneer het waterniveau de sensor bereikt, gaat er stroom door het water. Dit wordt door het regelsysteem gedetecteerd.

tekst: Temperatuurbeveiliging / clixon De temperatuurbeveiliging (of clixon) beschermt de verwarming tegen oververhitting als het regelsysteem de verwarming niet uitschakelt. De beveiliging onderbreekt de stroomtoevoer naar de verwarming onmiddellijk als de boiler te heet wordt. De beveiliging is een behuizing met een bimetalen schijf. Als het apparaat te heet wordt, opent de bimetalen schijf een (in rusttoestand gesloten) schakelaar. Interne delen van de temperatuurbeveiliging 1. Schakelarm 2. Transferpin 3. Basis 4. Schijfbevestiging 5. Kap 6. Bimetalen schijf Na het afkoelen kan de veiligheidsschakelaar worden gereset door handmatig op de pin (1) te drukken. Waardes temperatuurbeveiliging Deze koffiemachine heeft één open boiler: De open boiler heeft twee verschillende clixons. • Een droogkookbeveiliging op het bovendeksel van de open boiler. Deze clixon schakelt uit wanneer de temperatuur boven de 110 °C ± 5 °C uitkomt. • Een temperatuurbeveiliging op de overloopleiding van de open boiler. Deze clixon schakelt uit wanneer de temperatuur van het overtollige water boven de 90 °C ± 5 °C uitkomt.
